title: CyTOF mass cytometry analysis of human memory CD4+ T cells and memory B cells
protocol: Collect vials of PBMCs from liquid nitrogen and place on dry ice.
Rapidly thaw the cells by placing the vials in a 37°C water bath until only a pea-sized piece of ice remains (1–2 min).
Transfer the contents of each vial to a pre-labeled 10 ml tube on ice.
Add 10 drops of cold PBMC media to each tube using a transfer pipette and gently flick to mix.
Repeat step adding 10 drops until the tube has been filled to 5 ml.
Use 1 ml of media from the 10 ml tube to rinse the cryovial and collect any remaining cells.
Place the cap on each tube and gently invert to mix.
Add 20 drops of cold PBMC media to each tube and gently flick to mix.
Repeat step adding 20 drops until tubes have been filled to 10 ml.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Thoroughly resuspend cells in 10 ml of cold PBMC media.
Place tubes on ice until remaining vials of PBMCs have been thawed.
Repeat steps collecting, thawing, and processing each additional vial as needed.
If cell clumps are observed, pass cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer to remove clumps before counting.
Add 10 μL of trypan blue to each well of a u-bottom 96-well plate.
Add 10 μL of cells to each well and pipette to mix.
Load 10 μL of the mixture into a hemacytometer.
Count cells and calculate the number of cells per sample.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Resuspend cells to a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL with PBMC media.
Transfer 1 mL (2 × 10^6 cells) of resuspended cells to a fresh 10 mL tube.
Place the tube on ice until ready to start the staining protocol.
Prepare Cell-ID Cisplatin by diluting 5 mM Cell-ID Cisplatin 1:1,000 in DPBS to make a 5 μM working stock.
Dilute Human TruStain FcX 1:10 in cell staining buffer.
Dilute each surface marker antibody in cell staining buffer as indicated.
Place all diluted reagents on ice until needed.
Add 2 mL of DPBS to each tube containing cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Add 200 μL of Cell-ID cisplatin to each tube.
Pipette to mix.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Note: Stain cells with Cell-ID cisplatin for a maximum of 5 minutes.
Add 2 mL of cell staining buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Add 50 μL of Fc receptor block to each tube.
Pipette to mix.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C) on an orbital mixer at 100 rpm.
Add 50 μL of antibody cocktail to each tube.
Pipette to mix.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C) on an orbital mixer at 100 rpm.
Add 2 mL of cell staining buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Repeat steps from adding Fc receptor block to centrifuging after antibody cocktail addition.
Vortex samples to thoroughly disrupt the cell pellets.
Add 1 mL of nuclear antigen staining buffer to each tube.
Vortex to mix.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 2 mL of nuclear antigen staining perm to each tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 800 g for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge cells at a higher speed after fixation to reduce cell loss.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Repeat steps of aspirating, flicking, and vortexing samples.
Vortex samples thoroughly to disrupt the cell pellets.
Add 50 μL of a 1:50 dilution 161Dy-conjugated anti-T-bet (clone 4B10) antibody to each tube.
Pipette to mix.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 2 mL of nuclear antigen staining perm to each tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 800 g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Flick the tubes to disrupt the cell pellets.
Repeat steps of aspirating, flicking, and vortexing samples.
Vortex samples thoroughly to disrupt the cell pellets.
Place cells on ice for 10 min.
Prepare the DNA intercalator by diluting 125 μM Cell-ID Intercalator-Ir 1:1,000 in Maxpar Fix and Perm Buffer to make a 125 nM working stock (prepare 1 mL/sample).
Add 1 mL of intercalator to each tube.
Vortex to mix.
Incubate at 4°C overnight (16–20 h).
Connect the nebulizer.
Switch on the heater, nebulizer gas and sample flow running ultra-pure water in CyTOF software.
Monitor droplet formation by spraying onto the underside of a cell culture dish lid.
Stop the sample instruction before mounting the nebulizer and when the heater temperature is >195°C.
Ignite the plasma.
Leave instrument to thermally stabilize for a minimum of 20 min.
Introduce a tube of tuning solution using the sample loader.
Monitor 159Tb dual count signal in masses per reading mode until it has stabilized.
Launch the full automated tuning protocol in tuning manager.
Ensure signal from 159Tb is >6 × 105 counts per pg.
Remove tuning solution and wash for 3–5 minutes with wash solution.
Wash again for 3–5 minutes with ultra-pure water.
Vigorously shake four element EQ bead bottle for 30 seconds.
Load a tube with 0.5 mL of beads into the sample loader.
Monitor bead rate using a rain plot with bead channels open until event rate has stabilized.
Collect 120 seconds of data.
Run clustering on the resulting EQ file in Process mode to identify main bead populations: 151Eu and 153Eu median signals should be >1,000 counts, total bead numbers should be >6000.
Load a tube of ultra-pure water into the sample loader and run until samples are ready for acquisition.
At the end of the day, after sample acquisition, run wash solution for 5 minutes.
Run ultra-pure water for an additional 5 minutes prior to shutting down the system.
Remove the nebulizer after washing.
Refill the nebulizer with ultra-pure water to avoid clogging in dry state.
Wash cell suspensions.
Retrieve fixed and stained cell suspensions from storage at 4°C.
Acquire approximately 400,000 events per sample for data collection.
Monitor cells to determine the number of useable events needed based on pre-processing steps such as doublet discrimination and viability gating.
Vigorously shake the storage bottle containing EQ beads for 30 seconds before use.
Aliquot 1 mL of bead suspension into water and transfer to a round-bottomed 5 mL snap-cap centrifuge tube.
Add 4 mL ultra-pure water to the tube, replace cap, and invert to mix.
Centrifuge at 1,000 g for 8 minutes at ambient temperature in a swinging bucket centrifuge.
Decant supernatant after centrifugation.
Gently flick cell pellet to resuspend.
Add 4 mL of ultra-pure water, replace tube cap, and invert to mix again.
Centrifuge at 1,000 g for 8 minutes at ambient temperature (20°C–25°C) in a swinging bucket centrifuge.
Decant supernatant after the second centrifugation.
Resuspend cells using pipetting to achieve approximately 0.75-1 × 10^6 cells per mL.
Filter resuspended cells through the mesh of a cell strainer tube immediately before acquisition.
Acquire sample on Helios.
Set up a template with all required parameters for the experiment.
Create a full mass range template to monitor for unexpected metal contamination.
Load sample and acquire in CyTOF software.
Collect .imd format files along with .fcs files.
Monitor the run using a rain plot.
Ensure stable sample delivery, absence of clogging, and absence of metal contamination.
Adjust event rate by pausing sample acquisition if necessary.
Add additional water/EQ mix to adjust event rate if needed.
Load a tube of ultra-pure water on the sample introduction system after data collection.
Monitor the event rate in Preview mode until it is less than 1 per second.
Run wash solution for 3 min between every 3–4 samples.
Run ultra-pure water for 3–5 min after wash solution to remove lanthanides adhering to the sample tubing.
Monitor event rate in Preview mode until it is <1 per second.
Prepare cell suspension samples throughout the day to avoid storage in pellet form for longer than necessary.
Prepare two samples of approximately 10^6 cells per sample at one time, overlapping preparation times so that when one set is finished running, the first sample of the next set is ready to acquire.
